headline: GOLD $4,416 REBOUND AHEAD OF FRIDAY NFP — XAU/USD Recovers 1% From $4,374 Low As Bond Yields Ease; Bulls Eye $4,450 Before Make-Or-Break Jobs Report
snippet: Gold staged a 1% recovery to $4,416 on Thursday September 3 — reversing Tuesday's slide to $4,374 and reclaiming H1 technical structure — as 10-year Treasury yields eased from their 4.79% peak, the ISM Services PMI came in softer than expected, and the US dollar index pulled back ahead of Friday's August Non-Farm Payrolls report. FXStreet's technical analysis identifies $4,440–$4,460 as the key resistance cluster; a clean break above that zone would signal the correction from January's $5,420 record is ending, with $4,500 the next meaningful target. The asymmetric setup: a weak payrolls print Friday collapses September rate-hike odds from their current 62–66% and could drive a 5–10% gold rally; a strong print re-tests $4,282 support. Gold equities have been outperforming spot gold this week — producers generating record free cash flow at $4,400+ are valued well below comparable earnings multiples in the broader equity market.

headline: ANZ: COPPER HEADING FOR RECORD AS TARIFF PANIC DISTORTS SHIPMENTS — Chile Output -9.4% In July; LME Spot Premium At 4-Year High With 42 Consecutive Stockpile Draws
snippet: ANZ Group Holdings told Bloomberg September 3 that copper has the scope to rise to a new all-time record as US tariff uncertainty distorts global metal flows — traders are front-loading deliveries into the US ahead of a potential Section 232 decision — while mine supply faces compounding pressure: Chile reported a 9.4% decline in copper output in July, extending the supply shortfalls that project a 442,000-tonne global deficit in 2026. Copper held near $6.52/lb as the LME spot premium sits at a 4-year high after 42 consecutive sessions of stockpile draws. Investment in electric vehicles and new-energy infrastructure continues to support consumption as South American supply faces ongoing challenges. For investors in copper exploration and development companies, ANZ's call is meaningful: the combination of tariff-induced physical market distortion, structural mine supply declines, and demand growth creates one of the strongest fundamental setups for copper equities seen in the current cycle.

headline: AZTEC MINERALS EXTENDS TOMBSTONE STRIKE 255m TO 1,250m — Arizona Oxide Gold Hits 83.8m At 1.31 g/t AuEq Including 7.6m At 8.34 g/t AuEq In Step-Outs
snippet: Aztec Minerals Corp. (TSXV: AZT) released September 2 results from five RC drill holes at the Tombstone Property in southeastern Arizona: best hole TR26-43 returned 83.8 metres at 1.31 g/t gold equivalent (0.90 g/t Au + 22.61 g/t Ag) from the Contention mineralised system, including 7.6 metres at 8.34 g/t AuEq — and all five step-out holes intersected oxide gold-silver mineralisation with no barren hole in between. The program extends the Contention system by 255 metres to over 1,250 metres of continuously-drilled strike on patented mining claims consolidated over the past year. Oxide gold at these grades and widths in Arizona is economically amenable to heap-leach processing, and Tombstone's mineral system scale and drill consistency are the profile that historically precedes a maiden NI 43-101 resource estimate as the next formal catalyst.

headline: VIOR GOLD SETS DEPTH RECORD AT LIGNERIS — 14.6 g/t AU Over 2m Incl. 29 g/t Au At Record 845m Depth In Abitibi; 85% Through 30,000m Program
snippet: Vior Gold Corporation released September 1 new assay results from the Ligneris Project in Quebec's Abitibi region: hole LI-26-035 returned 14.6 g/t gold over 2.0 metres including 29.0 g/t Au over 1.0 metre, and hole LI-26-038 returned 6.43 g/t Au over 4.9 metres from the deepest intercept ever recorded at Ligneris — 845 vertical metres. With approximately 25,500 metres drilled in the 2026 program and 2,600+ assay samples still pending at the laboratory, the high-grade footprint continues to grow toward an updated resource estimate. Depth extension past 800 metres without grade degradation is the technical result that supports underground mine planning and is a key milestone before commissioning a resource update in the world's most gold-prolific geological terrane.

headline: LAHONTAN SANTA FE STOCKPILE DRILL COMPLETE — 10.7m At 1.81 g/t AU And 64.8 g/t Ag Validates Nevada Heap-Leach Economics At $4,300+ Gold
snippet: Lahontan Gold Corp. (TSXV: LG) announced September 1 the completion of its Santa Fe Mine stockpile diamond drilling program in Nevada, with the best interval returning 10.7 metres at 1.81 g/t gold and 64.8 g/t silver. The program tested heap-leach amenability of mineralised material on existing mine stockpiles at the historic Santa Fe Mine — an approach that allows rapid permitting and potentially low-capital early production from already-disturbed ground without requiring a new open pit. At gold above $4,300/oz and silver above $65/oz, the economic threshold for processing legacy oxide stockpiles in Nevada has dropped significantly compared with prior gold price cycles. The Santa Fe stockpile grades are the technical result needed before commissioning a preliminary economic assessment of the heap-leach option.

headline: ESGOLD SPINS FIRST DRILL AT MONTAUBAN QUEBEC — 5,000m / 29 Holes Target Historic Silver-Lead-Zinc-Gold Camp 120km West Of Quebec City
snippet: ESGold Corp. (TSXV: ESAU) announced September 3 the commencement of its 2026 surface diamond drilling program at the Montauban Project in Quebec, approximately 120 kilometres west of Quebec City: 5,000 metres across 29 proposed drill holes principally targeting the historic Montauban mine area. Montauban was a past-producing polymetallic mine with silver, lead, zinc, and gold mineralisation — a multi-revenue-stream profile highly attractive at current commodity prices. ESGold is testing the geological model developed from historical mining records and recent surface geophysics, with assay results expected in coming weeks. First-pass drilling at a well-mineralised historic Quebec camp is the catalyst that converts geological prospectivity into investor-grade data, and the polymetallic profile means that even a modest discovery could carry economics strengthened by four independent commodity revenue streams.

headline: CYGNUS METALS AND CAML: TSX CONDITIONALLY APPROVES UNIFIED LISTING — ASX/TSXV Explorer Merges With London-Listed Copper-Zinc Producer Central Asia Metals
snippet: The Toronto Stock Exchange conditionally approved the listing of Central Asia Metals (CAML) shares September 1, clearing the final major exchange requirement for the Scheme of Arrangement between Cygnus Metals Limited (ASX: CY5 / TSXV: CYG) and London-listed CAML — a cash-flow-generating copper-zinc-lead producer with operating mines in Kazakhstan (Kounrad copper) and North Macedonia (Sasa zinc-lead). The combined entity will trade on the TSX under the symbol 'CAML,' giving Canadian retail investors direct-exchange access to a producing base metals company with consistent free cash flow alongside Cygnus's exploration-stage growth assets. The deal reflects the ongoing trend of M&A consolidation in the base metals sector, with producers using strong balance sheets built during the copper cycle to acquire diversified mineral asset portfolios.

headline: SEPTEMBER TO REMEMBER: SEASONAL GOLD/SILVER SETUP, NFP ASYMMETRY, AND WHY Q4 May Be The Year's Best Entry — SGT Report
snippet: SGT Report's September 3 analysis argues that retail precious metals investors face one of the most asymmetric seasonal setups in years: gold and silver have been beaten down by Fed rate-hike fear from their January records while their structural bull case — sovereign debt, central bank accumulation, six-year silver deficit, and geopolitical gold demand — remains completely intact. The piece maps the NFP decision tree: a soft jobs print Friday collapses hike pricing and drives a 5–10% metals rally, while a strong print is already largely priced into spot (gold is down 20% from the January $5,420 record). Seasonal data from 25 years of gold bull markets shows that late-summer corrections into autumn harvest demand and Indian wedding season have consistently marked the best entry points of each calendar year — and this September, with miners at historically cheap P/E ratios vs. their own cash flows, the magnitude of the potential re-rating is unusually large.

headline: SILVER HITS TWO-MONTH HIGH $65.88 ON SEPT 3 — Dollar Softens Ahead Of NFP; Six-Year Physical Deficit Unchanged; $80+ Target Unchanged Despite Fed Noise
snippet: Silver rose 0.87% to $65.88 per troy ounce on September 3 — approximately a two-month high — as the US dollar softened ahead of Friday's NFP data, with the metal recovering 1.7% from last week's $64.76 low. The daily price movement is secondary to the unchanged structural picture: the Silver Institute projects the sixth consecutive annual supply deficit in 2026 at 46.3 million ounces, and China reclassified silver as a strategic material effective January 1, 2026, creating new export licensing requirements. Silver's 47% decline from the January record of $121.79 has been entirely driven by the Fed rate-hike narrative with no change in the physical supply-demand balance. For investors in silver-leveraged junior explorers and royalty companies — valued against an artificially depressed price denominator — the asymmetric trade is that the structural drivers persist whether Friday's NFP beats or misses.
